title: About the Knolls
lede: A small rural community in the hills of eastern Simi Valley, Ventura County.

sections.heading: The neighborhood
sections.text:
The Santa Susana Knolls straddles the hills (the “knolls”) at the foot of the Santa Susana Mountains, on the Simi Valley side. It is an unincorporated area of Ventura County, which means county agencies, not the City of Simi Valley, handle services such as law enforcement, roads and planning.

Our streets and lanes wind around the hills, and the city's street grid stops at the railroad crossings at the edge of the neighborhood. Homes sit among oak trees and sandstone boulders on lots of every shape and size, so even though shopping and the 118 freeway are only minutes away, the Knolls still feels like a small rural community.

Wildlife is part of daily life here: roadrunners, quail, red-tailed hawks, screech owls and the occasional California king snake. Many residents keep horses, and the oak trees and sandstone outcroppings give the Knolls its character.

sections.heading: A little history
sections.text:
Artifacts found in the open land across the tracks from the train depot show that people have lived in this area since long before the Spanish era.

The community grew up around the railroad. The Santa Susana Depot opened in 1903 and was moved in 1975 to its current home on Katherine Road, where it now houses a railroad museum and a public meeting room.

In the 20th century, the Hollywood film community kept getaway cabins in the Knolls. Many classic Westerns and action films were shot among the rocky outcroppings of nearby Corriganville. When Simi Valley incorporated as a city in 1969, the Knolls stayed outside the city limits and remains part of unincorporated Ventura County today.
sections.image_alt: A rock and stone archway at a Knolls home
sections.caption: Hand-built stonework on a Knolls lane.

sections.heading: The Homeowners Association
sections.text:
The Santa Susana Knolls Homeowners Association was founded in 1969, when the City of Simi Valley incorporated. Unlike most HOAs, it was not started by a developer and does not maintain common areas. Residents formed it to keep the Knolls a close-knit, rural community and to give neighbors a shared voice on matters that affect the area.

The HOA is a registered California non-profit run by volunteer neighbors. New to the Knolls? Come to an HOA meeting at the Depot. It's the easiest way to meet your neighbors. See the board and meeting schedule.
